As the emitter-anode distance, d and the anode radius, R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub> are much greater than r<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, the electric field in vacuum may be computed using the method of electrostatic images.

articleTitle: Energy exchange in field emission from semiconductors
abstract: In order to evaluate the energy exchange in field emission, we have investigated the replacement of electrons. The occupied energy levels near the surface are emptied by tunneling of electron through the surface barrier. They are reoccupied with electrons supplied from the back contact. This replacement process in the emitting region is not usually considered in the description of field emission. However, it has to be taken into account to evaluate the energy gain or loss of the cathode during the complete process of field emission. This energy exchange, the so-called Nottingham effect, changes from one of heating to one of cooling at the inversion temperature where the net energy exchange per electron is zero.Recently we have formulated the replacement process for semiconductor. The energy exchange is the difference between the average energies of the field and replacement electrons.

articleTitle: Field emission from vertically aligned silicon nanotubes
abstract: In the present work, diamond nanoparticles were used as nanomasks for SiNTs fabrication. The diamond nanoparticles with a diameter of about 100 nm were uniformly dispersed on the surface of a Si wafer as masks. The SiNTs were synthesized through a dry etching processing in an inductively coupled plasma (ICP) system. It is concluded that the field emission characteristics of the SiNTs has been performed, the turn-on the threshold fields for field electron emission are -7.9 MV/m and -13.6 MV/m, respectively.

articleTitle: Efficiency of surface conduction electron emission from ZnO nanostructure
abstract: In this paper, we study the influence of the ZnO nanostructures, gap between cathode and gate, resistance of ZnO layer, and the accelerate electric field on the ration of Ia/Ig. Fig.3 gives the variation of gate current and anode current with different cathode-gate distance. From these curves, the electron emission efficiency can be estimated.

articleTitle: Local field emission characteristic of individual AIN cone fabricated by focused ion beam
abstract: In summary, an individual AlN cone with high aspect ratio was formed by FIB technique. And a nature field emission property of individual AlN cone was measured in a dual probe SEM system. The results indicated that as formed single AlN cone with high aspect ratio exhibits a good field emission ability without any field shielding effect although only has a tiny emission area. Compared with a single Si cone fabricated by the same method, a single AlN cone has a better electron emission ability and hence a good promising candidate of point electron source candidate for the application of vacuum electronic device field.

articleTitle: The concept of Suppressor-less Schottky emitter
abstract: In a Schottky emitter, the useful emission comes from the W (100) facet at the very end of the tip. The emission from all other parts of the tip called shank emission is suppressed by a suppressor electrode. This paper discusses the simulation results by SIMION for the Suppressor-less Schottky emitter model.

articleTitle: Field emission properties of ZnO nanowire array directly grown from zinc substrate
abstract: ZnO nanowires were grown by direct oxidation of ZnO substrate. The field emission from ZnO nanowire has been studied. The obtained results indicated that the ZnO nanowire has good field emission properties.

articleTitle: Electron emission properties of silicon field emitter arrays in gaseous ambient for charge compensation device
abstract: Field emitter arrays made of silicon (Si-FEAs) is a possible candidate for the space charge compensation device during ion implantation process for semiconductor devices, because they are free from metal contamination and have less out-gas. When operating in the ion implanter, Si-FEAs suffer from the pressure increase due to out-gassing from resist materials on a silicon wafer. We examined electron emission properties of the Si-FEAs in H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>, CO, O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, or CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> ambient, which are gases resulting from ion implantation to photoresist. In the work of Gotoh et al. (2006), Si-FEAs treated by CHF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> plasma (Si:C-FEA) were also examined. As a result, it was found that O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> ambient shortened the lifetime of the Si-FEA, but not for the lifetime of the Si:C-FEA. On the other hand, reductive ambient produced good properties of electron emission. In this study, we examined the lifetime of the Si-FEA and the Si:C-FEA in O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> ambient again to reproduce the previous result, and also the lifetime in C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> which is also one of the major gases in the implantation ambient.

articleTitle: Enhanced field emission properties from ZnO nanostructure by improving contact behavior
abstract: According to previous reports, field emission properties mainly depend on the shape or the aspect ratio of ZnO nanostructure materials[1][2]. However, besides above two parameters, the contact property between the ZnO nanostructural emitters and substrates is also an important parameter determining the field emission properties. It is considered that moderate substrate materials may induce the formation of the good Ohmic contact between the ZnO nanostructures and the substrates. Recently, only a few reports discussed field emission properties from the ZnO nanostructures with consideration of the contact behavior, but no one discussed the contact effect on field emission properties of the emitters which are screen-printed on the substrate. In this paper, we have studied the contact effect on the field emission properties of ZnO nanostructure printed on various substrates to understand emission performance more exactly.

articleTitle: Fabrication of aligned CNT bundle emitters in different density
abstract: Aligned CNT bundle emitters in different density are prepared by MPCVD. The reaction pressure is the most important factor, which is responsible for the density of CNT bundles. Based on our results, the etching time of the H2 plasma has much effect on the aligned growth of the CNT bundles. Controlled growth of the aligned CNT bundles in different density is necessary for the application of CNTs in FETs. Further measurements on the FE properties of the CNT bundles in different density are still on research.

articleTitle: Field emitter arrays for tomographic medical imaging
abstract: We are developing a new stationary X-ray source for tomographic imaging with the potential to revolutionize tomographic imaging technology. Energy analysis of the X-ray output has shown clean spectra using both molybdenum and tungsten anodes. At present a prototype system is being assembled for tomographic imaging of small animals for medical research. This paper discusses the results of the X-ray source experiments and plans for the further development of stationary, multiple-source, tomographic imaging systems.

articleTitle: Fabrication and field emission properties of gated field emitter arrays with hafnium nitride cathode
abstract: We fabricated the FEAs of which emitters are covered with HfN films, and showed relatively good electron emission properties including lifetime and operation at the elevated temperatures up to 100degC. The fabricated device showed relatively good electron emission properties. Typically, electron emission started at V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">EG</sub> of about 40 V, and the current of 1 muA was observed at V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">EG</sub> of 60 V. Some of the 2,025-tip FEA yielded a high current of 100 muA at V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">EG</sub> of 120 V.

articleTitle: Exact mathematical solution for the principal field emission correction function υ used in Standard Fowler-Nordheim theory
abstract: In summary, this work puts the mathematics of the Schottky-Nordheim barrier onto a more complete and fully respectable basis. It also opens the way to new developments.

articleTitle: Tutorial lecture on the theory of cold field electron emission
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present models of electron emission that bridge basic concepts to their computational realization in emission models. Emphasis is placed on the relation of field emission to the other emission mechanisms, in particular thermal and photoemission. A number of complications and modifications to the Canon of Field Emission arise because of particulars related to electron sources and how they are used.

articleTitle: Development of a vacuum packaged nanodiamond lateral field emission device
abstract: Vacuum microelectronic devices involving lateral-type emitters offer reduced complexity for device integration and vacuum packaging. In addition, their small interelectrode separation feature results in low voltage device operation, essential for practical microelectronic applications. Utilizing the properties of CVD nanocrystalline diamond, we have demonstrated a lateral field emission device capable of functioning efficiently at both low and high temperatures (200 degC), with an inherent "hardness" to radiation exposure as high as 15 Mrad(SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) total dose (Kang, et.al., 2007). The development of a vacuum package is of practical relevance to field emission devices. We report the development of the first diamond lateral field emitter device operating in a vacuum package.

articleTitle: Role of dielectric for field emission at the metal-dielectric-vacuum triple junction
abstract: In this paper the field emission enhancement at the dielectric-metal contact is theoretically investigated. Even though such a strange phenomenon as vacuum breakdown has been reported for half a century, it is not understood well. However, it has been considered to result from the enhancement of the electric field near the metal-dielectric-vacuum triple junction. Recently it has been argued that the field enhancement is due to the combined effect of the surface charge of metal and the polarization of dielectric. The two opposite charge densities causes each other to become a saturation value. Then the field intensity near the triple junction can be stronger than that in the absence of dielectric.

articleTitle: Characteristics of nanosilicon ballistic cold cathode in liquids as an active electrode
abstract: This paper reports a concept of the ballistic emitter operation for its possible use in liquids. The nc-Si cold cathodes were fabricated on n-type Si wafers or polycrystalline Si films. It is concluded that the ballistic emitter provides useful means not only for hydrogen generation, but also for control of pH values, redox potentials, and electrochemical activity of solutions including biological media.
